title: Decision Entry
description: One entry in the cross-agent decision log (charter primitive: decision log). The minimum content a future agent — different model, different session, different device — needs to rely on the decision without re-asking the operator. Append-only: written by scripts/decisions.sh add and validated on every append. Each line of decisions.jsonl is one such entry.

schema_version.description: Per-entry schema version so future format bumps stay backward-readable. Cheap to carry, expensive to retrofit.

id.description: sha256 hex digest of the canonical body: this object with the 'id' field removed, serialized as JSON with sort_keys=true and separators=(',', ':'). Stable and content-addressed: two identical decisions get the same id, which makes deduplication trivial and supersedes-pointers reliable.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the decision was recorded (e.g. '2026-05-25T22:30:00Z').

adapter.description: Which adapter wrote this entry. Workers write under their own token; the operator runs `decisions.sh add --adapter human`.

author.description: Optional free-form author identifier. Primarily for human-attested decisions (e.g. 'operator') or to distinguish multiple operators.

repo.description: Scope of this decision: repo basename (from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), or 'global' for cross-repo decisions, or 'unknown' when no git repo could be detected. Lets agents filter the log to decisions that apply to the project they're working in.

decision.description: 1-2 sentence statement of what was decided. The fact.

why.description: 1-2 sentence statement of the constraint, deadline, prior incident, or charter rule that drove it. The load-bearing field — without 'why' a future agent will second-guess and may silently reverse the decision.

refs.description: Free-form pointer strings for traceability. Suggested shapes (not enforced for M8.0): 'task:task-abc', 'commit:6581b40', 'doc:CHARTER.md', 'M7.2', 'PR:https://...'. Typed refs may land in a later slice; until then, agents grep these strings.
